ValidationViolation::new.signature: pub fn new( unit: ValidationUnit, location: ValidationLocation, message: impl Into<String>, severity: ValidationSeverity, ) -> Self
ValidationViolation::new.body: { Self { unit, location, message: message.into(), severity, } }
ValidationViolation::new.obligation: Own exact supplied unit, location and severity; invoke message Into<String> once and preserve its converted string. No severity filtering, sanitization or implicit mathematical check. Caller-provided conversion behavior is not assumed pure or terminating.

ValidationResult::pass.body: { Self { unit: unit.into(), passed: true, violations: Vec::new(), } }
ValidationResult::pass.obligation: Store exact unit, passed=true and empty message vector. This is caller metadata, not an executed test.

ValidationResult::fail.signature: pub fn fail(unit: &str, violations: Vec<String>) -> Self
ValidationResult::fail.body: { Self { unit: unit.into(), passed: false, violations, } }
ValidationResult::fail.obligation: Store exact unit and owned message vector with passed=false, even if messages are empty.

ValidationReport::new.body: { Self { target_name: name.into(), results: Vec::new(), typed_violations: Vec::new(), } }
ValidationReport::new.obligation: Store exact target name and empty vectors. Empty report is vacuously passing; names are unvalidated metadata.

ValidationReport::add.signature: pub fn add(&mut self, result: ValidationResult)
ValidationReport::add.obligation: Append one supplied raw result unchanged. Public passed/messages fields may contradict; only passed flags enter success/failure counts.

ValidationReport::add_violation.signature: pub fn add_violation(&mut self, violation: ValidationViolation)
ValidationReport::add_violation.obligation: Append one failed result with exact Debug unit name and cloned message, then move the complete typed issue to typed_violations. Error/Warning/Info all block all_passed. Type renderer is diagnostic text, not a stable wire format.

ValidationReport::add_typed.signature: pub fn add_typed(&mut self, unit: &str, violations: Vec<ValidationViolation>)
ValidationReport::add_typed.body: { if violations.is_empty() { self.results.push(ValidationResult::pass(unit)); } else { let messages = violations .iter() .map(|violation| violation.message.clone()) .collect(); self.results.push(ValidationResult::fail(unit, messages)); self.typed_violations.extend(violations); } }
ValidationReport::add_typed.obligation: Empty batch appends exactly one passing result and no typed issue. Nonempty batch appends one failed result named by the separate batch unit, projects messages in input order and moves complete typed issues in that same order. Batch unit need not equal issue units; failure_count counts result rows, not individual issues.

ValidationReport::all_passed.obligation: Return all stored flags true AND typed vector empty. Short circuit has no side effects. Messages/severity are not inferred as flags; public contradictory fields do not become certificates.

ValidationReport::failure_count.obligation: Count false result flags only. Count is at most results.len(), hence fits actual usize Vec length; no sum of unbounded external counts.

ValidationReport::violation_count.obligation: Return exactly typed_violations.len(), independent of result row count and severity.

invariant_argument: ValidationInventory models unrestricted flags/issues, exact append/projection, vacuous success, typed blockers and bounded failure counts. Rust Vec preserves list order, clones only necessary owned projections, and count cannot exceed actual Vec length. Unit Debug rendering and std allocation are separately reviewed runtime contracts.

ArrowEffects is a pure total mathematical callback value model over Reader, owned State, ordered List writer and Except. Compose associativity is proved in that model only. Rust Fn does not imply purity, termination, panic freedom or determinism. Concrete source control flow and native traces establish invocation order/short circuit and original error payloads under admitted runtime callbacks; no blanket runtime category-law or rollback theorem.

Fanout model accepts an arbitrary clone function; successful left input is clone(a) and right input is a. The non-lawful Odd clone fixture detects swapped clone/original delivery. Context rationals are opaque stored input: even raw 1/0 or 2/4 is transported without normalization or arithmetic by these combinators.
